    Referral safeguarding reminder

    • Share only the minimum information needed for a safe referral, with appropriate consent and access controls.
    • Track timeliness and outcomes using approved protocols; avoid exposing sensitive case details in public dashboards.
    • Disaggregate only where safe, useful, and consistent with data-protection and survivor-centred principles.

    Trends & analysis

    Analytical signals to support operational discussion—not a substitute for contextual validation.

    Feedback by sector

    Reported topic/sector, illustrative distribution

    Feedback by channel

    How feedback reached the mechanism

    Interpretation notes

    • High feedback volume may reflect easier access to a channel, stronger awareness, or increased concern; it does not automatically indicate poorer service quality.
    • Low complaint volume should not be interpreted as satisfaction without checking awareness, accessibility, trust, inclusion, and safety.
    • Closure rate is a process indicator. It does not by itself establish that the affected person considers the response adequate.
    • Any operational decisions should triangulate feedback with service data, partner knowledge, context, and community consultation.

    Geographic interpretation

    • Higher volume can reflect access to channels, partner presence, population, or community awareness—not necessarily poorer service quality.
    • Compare with estimated reach, channel availability, service coverage, and safe qualitative feedback.
    • Small counts and sensitive categories may require suppression to reduce re-identification risk.

    Hub composition

    The 14 governorates are assigned to the four hubs as specified for this portfolio.
